This formula treats dysenteric disorders due to damp-heat in the Yang Brightness Qi aspect. In this pattern, the exterior has not been completely relased, but the interior is already ablaze with heat. This can be caused by improper treatment of an exterior disorder with purgatives. A pathogen in the interior may or not present. Heat is more severe than dampness. This formula is appropiate where the prolapse occurs as a result of heat excess diarrhea.

Chief: Bai tou weng (Rx Pulsatillae) clears damp-heat and relieves fire toxin, especially in the blood level.

Deputy: Huang lian (Rz Coptidis) clears damp-heat from stomach and intestine and Huang bai (Cx Phellodendri) clears damp-heat from the lower burner.

Assistant: Qin pi (Cx Fraxini) drains dampness, resolves toxicity, and stops diarrhea.

3-Peony Decoction (shao yao tang)

The primary emphasis of this formula is to clear heat, dry dampness, and regulate Qi and Blood in order to guide out the cause of the disorder.

Chief: Huang lian (Rz Coptidis) and Huang qing (Rx Scutellariae), which resolve heat toxicity in the intestines by clearing heat and drying dampness.

Deputy: Da huang (Rhei Radix et Rhizoma), serves as the deputy to drain heat toxins through the stool. Shao yao (Rx Paeoniae), used in large dose to move the blood, expel the pus, relax urgency, and stop the pain. Dang gui (Rx Angelica sinensis), tonifies, warms, and moves the blood. Together, they regulate the nutritive Qi and Blood. When combined with Gan cao (Rx Glycyrrhizae), Shao yao (Rx Paeoniae) also moderates spasms and relieves abdominal pain.

Assistant: Rou gui (Cx Cinnamomi), this herbs enters the blood level and assists the blood-harmonizing herbs in moving the blood. It also acts as an opposing assistant, which means that it prevents the cold, bitter properties of the other herbs from either injuring the Yang or constraining the pathogenic influences in the interior and thereby transforming into smoldering damp-heat. The other assistants, Mu xiang (Rx Aucklandiae) and Bing lang (Sm Arecae), promote the movement of Qi and help eliminate stagnation.
